shadcn.label: shadcn/ui
avoidWhen: unstyled behavior primitive is the only need

radix.label: Radix UI
avoidWhen: complete visual surface is needed without a styling layer

foundation.reason: Own the hero shell, CTA, cards, and tokens with a stable styled foundation.

behavior.when: Only if the hero includes a dialog, popover, menu, or focus-sensitive control.

expression.reason: Use one headline reveal and one quiet proof focus treatment, never a gallery of effects.

reject: Radix alone: it supplies behavior, not the styled hero surface.
AnimatedList: the hero promise is not a result list.
FlowingMenu: it would spend the viewport's signature budget on navigation spectacle.

foundation.reason: Keep tables, filters, cards, and states under one token and density system.

behavior.when: Use for filter menus, dialogs, tooltips, switches, and keyboard-visible focus.

expression.reason: Data reading and repeated actions take priority over expressive motion.

reject: React Bits or Vue Bits as the default layer: reveal effects compete with scan speed.
TiltedCard: pointer depth does not help users compare records.
FlowingMenu: navigation spectacle slows a high-frequency workflow.

foundation.reason: Keep navigation, buttons, cards, and case-study scaffolding consistent.

behavior.when: Use only where the site has overlays, menus, or keyboard-sensitive interaction.

expression.reason: A portfolio can spend more delight budget on one authored media or showcase moment.

reject: Radix as the visual layer: primitives need a product surface around them.
CountUp without a meaningful proof metric: it becomes decorative.
Multiple signature effects in one viewport: the work loses authorship and hierarchy.

foundation.reason: Keep the landing shell, CTA, proof blocks, and tokens coherent.

behavior.when: Only when navigation, pricing toggles, dialogs, or focus-sensitive controls need primitives.

expression.reason: Spend expression on the product promise or one proof moment, not on every section.

reject: Dashboard motion patterns: repeated metrics and filters do not belong in a sparse marketing surface.
Multiple signature effects: they compete with the product promise.
CountUp without a truthful proof metric: it becomes decorative.

foundation.reason: Preserve the editor's existing surface, shortcut, and token language.

behavior.when: Use for command menus, popovers, dialogs, tooltips, and focus management.

expression.reason: Typing, selection, and keyboard completion take priority over expressive motion.

reject: React Bits or Vue Bits as the default layer: reveal effects interrupt editing.
TiltedCard: pointer depth adds no value to authoring.
FlowingMenu: animated navigation competes with keyboard-driven work.

foundation.reason: Keep forms, tables, status surfaces, and density under one product foundation.

behavior.when: Use for filters, dialogs, dropdowns, tooltips, switches, and keyboard focus.

expression.reason: Operational scanning and repeated actions should remain immediate.

reject: React Bits or Vue Bits as the default layer: expression competes with operations.
SpotlightCard: pointer focus does not improve record comparison.
FlowingMenu: navigation spectacle slows the admin workflow.

foundation.reason: Use the host's responsive primitives and preserve its mobile token language.

behavior.when: Use existing touch and navigation primitives; add Radix only for React overlays that need it.

expression.reason: Touch targets, content fit, and network-friendly rendering take priority.

reject: Desktop-first showcase effects: they often break touch and content fit.
TiltedCard: pointer depth is not a reliable mobile interaction.
Always-on motion: it consumes attention and battery without a product job.

foundation.reason: Keep navigation, code surfaces, callouts, and content tokens consistent.

behavior.when: Use for search, menus, dialogs, tabs, and focus-sensitive navigation.

expression.reason: Reading and wayfinding should remain calm and predictable.

reject: Hero reveal as the default: documentation value comes from findability and comprehension.
TiltedCard: perspective motion adds noise to code and reference content.
FlowingMenu: animated navigation harms fast wayfinding.

foundation.reason: Own plan cards, comparison states, CTAs, and tokens with a stable foundation.

behavior.when: Use for billing-period toggles, dialogs, tooltips, and keyboard-visible focus.

expression.reason: Pricing clarity and trust are more important than decorative movement.

reject: CountUp without a truthful price or usage transition: it can obscure the offer.
TiltedCard: perspective competes with plan comparison.
Multiple signature effects: conversion choices need stable scanning.

foundation.reason: Keep prompts, outputs, panels, and system states under one usable foundation.

behavior.when: Use for command menus, model pickers, dialogs, popovers, and focus management.

expression.reason: Use system motion for generation state; do not add gallery-style expression to the workspace.

reject: React Bits or Vue Bits as the default layer: work completion and state clarity come first.
FlowingMenu: animated navigation competes with prompt and output flow.
SpotlightCard on every output: repeated pointer focus becomes visual noise.
